Key rationale:
**1. The ping-based communication layer from build 31 does not handle bulk data transmission — it sends 64-byte ping packets and measures RTT. The TCP socket implementation built at build 31 is a raw socket layer that handles connection management, serialization, and streaming (it uses a `send_all()` / `recv_all()` pattern that handles arbitrary-size payloads by prefixing each message with a 4-byte length header). The 192 KB bootstrap packet was implemented at build 33 as part of the streaming latency gate, and the per‑tile LOD mesh transmission (variable size, up to ~16 KB per tile) is scheduled for build 34.**

The dependency chain (commit `a3f7c9f2`) was clarified further at build 33 after the question identified the gap between the ping probe's 64-byte packets and the protocol's 192 KB payloads. The build-31 bandwidth probe is only the raw socket foundation — it provides `tcp_send(sock, data)` and `tcp_recv(sock, size)` primitives that prefix each message with a 4-byte little-endian length header and then send/receive the full payload in a loop (`while bytes_sent < len(data): bytes_sent += sock.send(data[bytes_sent:])`). The 192 KB bootstrap packet transmission was implemented at build 33 as a separate layer (`protocol/bootstrap.py`) that uses the raw socket to send the full bootstrap payload — this layer was tested at build 33 with an actual 192 KB payload and verified that `recv_all()` correctly reassembles the data across multiple TCP segments. The per‑tile LOD mesh transmission (build 34) will use the same `send_all()` / `recv_all()` pattern. The optimization at build 36 can begin because the full data pipeline (socket + bootstrap + LOD selection) is in place by build 35.
